question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births registered in Taiwan in September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics.

target.what: Number of live births registered in Taiwan (Republic of China) during September 2026, as counted in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics (births registered in the month, by date of registration)
target.publisher: Ministry of the Interior (MOI), Department of Household Registration, Taiwan
target.cadence: monthly, published with roughly a 1-2 month lag after month end
target.caveats: Target period is future/incomplete relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no September 2026 figure exists yet; must be projected. Definition is registered births in the month (registration date basis), which can differ from births by occurrence date due to registration lag; MOI monthly statistics rep

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 registered births will follow the recent level and seasonal pattern of monthly registered births; the most recent months before the cutoff (e.g., Jan-Jul 2026) anchor the level, and prior Septembers give the September seasonal factor relative to adjacent months.
candidates.data_to_find: MOI monthly births registered for each month of 2023, 2024, 2025 and Jan-Jul (or latest available) 2026; specifically September values for 2023-2025 and the immediately preceding months (Jul-Aug) of 2026. Minimum: latest 12-24 monthly values plus 3 prior Septembers.

candidates.hypothesis: Alternative official series (DGBAS, National Development Council population projections, Directorate-General of Budget) report monthly or annual births that track MOI registered births with a stable ratio; these can cross-check and fill the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly or annual live births from DGBAS/NDC for 2024-2026, and the historical ratio to MOI registered births; latest 2026 monthly births if published.

assessment.note: All three give September 2025 registered births = 8,603; p1 is a news report, p16/p42 are MOI/RIS monthly-statistics extracts. Same underlying MOI measurement, so this is one source, not three independent confirmations.
Both describe the same September 2025 year-on-year decline (-27.04%, -3,189 births); internally consistent with 8,603 vs ~11,792 in September 2024. Same article, same source.
Crude birth rate and minutes-per-birth are arithmetic restatements of the 8,603 monthly count and population; they add no independent information about the level.
Monthly 2025 values from the same MOI/RIS table; they sum consistently to the 107,812 annual total (p43). This is the primary series for level and seasonality.
Duplicate statements of 2024 annual births = 134,856; same source, one data point.
The -20.05% change is consistent with 107,812 vs 134,856; same MOI table.
All three report 2025 TFR = 0.695 from MOI statistics; p30/p38 are NDC restatements of the same MOI figure, not independent measurements.

2026 first-7-month births ~54,000 is consistent with a continuation of the 2025 monthly level (~9,000/month) and with the steep 2025-2026 decline; it is the key 2026 anchor but is a rounded news citation.
NDC 2024 projection TFR assumptions (0.8-1.3) are far above realised 0.695; they are scenario parameters, not forecasts of the actual level, and should not be used as central anchors.

Marriage series is internally consistent (monthly sums to annual). It is a lagged conception proxy only; the December 2025 conception window maps to September 2026 births, but the marriage-to-birth link is weak and noisy.
Oct-Dec 2025 monthly births duplicate p19-p21; same source.
Death statistics are internally consistent but irrelevant to the birth target except as demographic context.
Migration and population-structure figures are consistent with each other but only contextual; they do not directly determine September 2026 births.

methods.rationale: Naive anchor: September 2025 registered births (8,603) as the most recent same-month value. Ignores the 2026 decline, so it is an upper-ish anchor; included as a backtestable baseline.

p16.role: September 2025 registered births in Taiwan (monthly MOI count)

a1.role: September seasonal factor relative to 2025 September

methods.rationale: Primary route: take the observed September 2025 level, apply the 2026 year-over-year decline implied by the ~54,000 first-7-month 2026 figure (p31), and a modest September seasonal adjustment. Shared dependency: both factors rest on the same MOI measurement basis; failure mode is that p31 is a rounded news citation and the 2026 decline could be steeper or shallower.

p31.role: Taiwan births first 7 months of 2026 (cumulative MOI-based)

a1.role: September seasonal factor relative to annual monthly mean

methods.rationale: Alternative route: annualize the 2026 first-7-month cumulative (p31) to a monthly average and apply the September seasonal factor. Independent of the 2025 September level, so it cross-checks m2; failure mode is the rounding of p31 and the assumption that H2 2026 tracks H1.

assumptions.name: September seasonal factor relative to 2025 September
assumptions.rationale: September 2026 is expected to have a similar seasonal position to September 2025; the 2025 monthly series shows September (8,603) close to the annual monthly mean (~8,984), so a factor near 1 with modest spread is appropriate. Uncertainty reflects single-year seasonality evidence.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the 2025 September level to 2026 September after applying the year-over-year level change.
assumptions.falsified_by: Multi-year data showing a strong systematic September seasonal spike or dip.

assumptions.name: 2026 vs 2025 year-over-year birth change factor
assumptions.rationale: 2026 first-7-month births (~54,000, p31) imply roughly 7,700/month vs 2025's ~8,984/month average, a ratio near 0.86; the continued fertility decline (TFR 0.695 in 2025) supports a further decline. Range spans a milder and a steeper continuation.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the 2025 September level to project the 2026 September level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Actual 2026 monthly MOI data showing the year-over-year ratio outside 0.75-0.95.

assessment.note: Same MOI September 2025 registered-birth count (8,603) reported by a news outlet and by the official household-registration table; they share one underlying measurement, so this is one fact, not three independent confirmations.
September 2025 was 27.04% / 3,189 births below September 2024; 8,603 + 3,189 = 11,792 matches p68, so the YoY figures and the 2024 level are internally consistent.
One continuous official 2025 monthly series from the same MOI table; mutually consistent and summing to the 107,812 annual total in p43.
2025 total 107,812 vs 2024 total 134,856 implies about -20.05%, matching the stated YoY change; consistent annual anchors.
Complete 2023 monthly MOI series; used only for the September seasonal shape, not for the 2026 level.
Complete 2024 monthly MOI series; September 2024 (11,792) is the base for the 2025 YoY drop and gives a second year of September seasonality.

2026 first-7-month cumulative of about 54,000 implies a monthly pace near 7,700, well below the 2025 monthly average of about 8,984; this is a genuine level decline, not a definitional conflict, and p31 is rounded to the nearest thousand.
TFR falling from 0.885 (2024) to 0.695 (2025) is consistent with the ~20% annual birth decline; both point to a continuing low 2026 level.

Marriage registrations fell ~15% in 2025 vs 2024; December 2025 marriages (p45) are the conception-window proxy for September 2026 births, but the marriage-to-birth link is weak and lagged, so this is contextual only.

methods.rationale: Naive seasonal anchor: September 2025 registered births (8,603) as the same-calendar-month baseline. Ignores the 2026 decline, so it is an upper-ish reference; backtested against prior Septembers.

p16.role: September 2025 registered births in Taiwan (monthly MOI count)

methods.rationale: Seasonal-anchor route: last September's count scaled by the 2026-vs-2025 level change implied by the 2026 year-to-date pace (p31) and the 2025 TFR decline. Shared dependency: both p16 and a2 rest on MOI registration data; failure mode is a change in registration timing.

p31.role: Taiwan births first 7 months of 2026 (cumulative MOI-based)

a3.role: number of months covered by the p31 cumulative (7)

a1.role: September seasonal factor relative to the 2026 monthly mean

methods.rationale: Level route: annualize the 2026 first-7-month cumulative (p31) to a monthly mean, then apply the September seasonal factor. p31 is rounded to the nearest thousand, so uncertainty is wide; failure mode is that the Jan-Jul pace differs from the Sep-Dec pace.

assumptions.name: September seasonal factor relative to the 2026 monthly mean
assumptions.rationale: September is typically slightly below the annual monthly mean in Taiwan's registration series: 2025 September (8,603) ≈ 0.96 of the 2025 monthly mean (8,984); 2024 September (11,792) ≈ 1.05 of the 2024 mean (11,238); 2023 September (10,717) ≈ 0.95 of the 2023 mean. Average ≈ 0.97, range spans observed year-to-year variation.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 monthly level is roughly flat across the year and September follows the historical seasonal shape.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 registration timing was shifted by holiday/typhoon closures or subsidy-driven registration bunching.

assumptions.name: 2026 vs 2025 year-over-year birth change factor
assumptions.rationale: 2026 first-7-month cumulative (~54,000, p31) implies a monthly pace near 7,700 versus 2025's ~8,984 monthly average, a ratio near 0.86; the 2025 TFR drop (p33) and falling marriages (p49 vs p50) support a continued decline rather than a rebound. Range reflects the rounding of p31 and uncertainty in the remaining months.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 level decline relative to 2025 persists through September.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly 2026 MOI data showing a level near or above 2025's monthly average.

assumptions.name: Months in the first-7-month cumulative window
assumptions.rationale: p31 covers January through July 2026, exactly seven calendar months; this is a calendar constant needed to convert the cumulative to a monthly mean.
assumptions.applies_when: p31 is the cumulative over January-July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that p31 covers a different number of months.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Naive seasonal anchor: September 2025 registered births (8,603) as the same-calendar-month baseline. Ignores the 2026 decline, so it is an upper-ish reference; backtested against prior Septembers.

methods.label: m2

p16.role: September 2025 registered births in Taiwan (monthly MOI count)

methods.rationale: Seasonal-anchor route: last September's count scaled by the 2026-vs-2025 level change implied by the 2026 year-to-date pace (p31) and the 2025 TFR decline. Shared dependency: both p16 and a2 rest on MOI registration data; failure mode is a change in registration timing.

methods.label: m3

p31.role: Taiwan births first 7 months of 2026 (cumulative MOI-based)

a3.role: number of months covered by the p31 cumulative (7)

a1.role: September seasonal factor relative to the 2026 monthly mean

methods.rationale: Level route: annualize the 2026 first-7-month cumulative (p31) to a monthly mean, then apply the September seasonal factor. p31 is rounded to the nearest thousand, so uncertainty is wide; failure mode is that the Jan-Jul pace differs from the Sep-Dec pace.
methods.error: formula: numeric constant 12 not allowed (only 1 and exponents); make it a named input. If the number only converts units (1000 g per kg, days per year), drop it and set the method's "unit" to the unit the formula then gives (e.g. 'g/day'); code converts it to 'birth'

kept.name: September seasonal factor relative to the 2026 monthly mean
kept.rationale: September is typically slightly below the annual monthly mean in Taiwan's registration series: 2025 September (8,603) ≈ 0.96 of the 2025 monthly mean (8,984); 2024 September (11,792) ≈ 1.05 of the 2024 mean (11,238); 2023 September (10,717) ≈ 0.95 of the 2023 mean. Average ≈ 0.97, range spans observ
kept.applies_when: The 2026 monthly level is roughly flat across the year and September follows the historical seasonal shape.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 registration timing was shifted by holiday/typhoon closures or subsidy-driven registration bunching.

kept.name: 2026 vs 2025 year-over-year birth change factor
kept.rationale: 2026 first-7-month cumulative (~54,000, p31) implies a monthly pace near 7,700 versus 2025's ~8,984 monthly average, a ratio near 0.86; the 2025 TFR drop (p33) and falling marriages (p49 vs p50) support a continued decline rather than a rebound. Range reflects the rounding of p31 and uncertainty in
kept.applies_when: The 2026 level decline relative to 2025 persists through September.
kept.falsified_by: Monthly 2026 MOI data showing a level near or above 2025's monthly average.

kept.name: Months in the first-7-month cumulative window
kept.rationale: p31 covers January through July 2026, exactly seven calendar months; this is a calendar constant needed to convert the cumulative to a monthly mean.
kept.applies_when: p31 is the cumulative over January-July 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that p31 covers a different number of months.

final.template:
The best computed estimate for registered live births in Taiwan during September 2026 (registration-date basis, MOI monthly household registration statistics) is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

Two methods were combined at [[m1_weight]] and [[m2_weight]]: a naive seasonal anchor using September 2025 births of [[p16_value]], and a seasonal-anchor route scaling that anchor by an assumed 2026-vs-2025 change factor of [[a2_value]] (range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]). The third method was unusable. The only observed inputs are [[p16_value]] and the first-[n]-month cumulative [[p31_value]]; the year-over-year factor is an assumption, not an observation. The weighting reflects the code's fixed scheme, not demonstrated backtest accuracy.

The main risk is a shift in registration timing or a change in the 2026 decline pace, which would move the scaled anchor. Better evidence would be actual monthly 2026 birth counts through August and any partial September registration data.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a2 2026 vs 2025 year-over-year birth change factor: [[a2_value]] ratio, range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Monthly 2026 MOI data showing a level near or above 2025's monthly average.
final.text:
The best computed estimate for registered live births in Taiwan during September 2026 (registration-date basis, MOI monthly household registration statistics) is 7,962 birth (80% model-based interval 5,779 to 10,969 birth).

Two methods were combined at 50% and 50%: a naive seasonal anchor using September 2025 births of 8,603 births, and a seasonal-anchor route scaling that anchor by an assumed 2026-vs-2025 change factor of 0.86 (range 0.7659 to 0.9573). The third method was unusable. The only observed inputs are 8,603 births and the first-[n]-month cumulative 54,000 births; the year-over-year factor is an assumption, not an observation. The weighting reflects the code's fixed scheme, not demonstrated backtest accuracy.

The main risk is a shift in registration timing or a change in the 2026 decline pace, which would move the scaled anchor. Better evidence would be actual monthly 2026 birth counts through August and any partial September registration data.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a2 2026 vs 2025 year-over-year birth change factor: 0.86 ratio, range 0.7659 to 0.9573 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Monthly 2026 MOI data showing a level near or above 2025's monthly average.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
